what_it_does: Quantum computers consist of delicate quantum bits (qubits) that must be continuously calibrated—tuning the microwave pulses that control them to ensure gates (quantum logic operations) execute accurately. Standard calibration runs operations one at a time sequentially, and it ignores that different qubits behave differently due to manufacturing tolerances. This paper presents a hardware-aware calibration protocol that first profiles how each pair of qubits responds to different waveforms (control signals), then assigns the right calibration strategy to each pair. Next, a graph algorithm identifies sets of calibration operations that don't interfere with each other and runs them in parallel, cutting total calibration time dramatically. The approach was validated on real IBM quantum hardware with up to 127 qubits.
